dedupe_keys.name: response times to fires attended by fire and rescue services england official statistics

description: This series of official statistics reports how long fire and rescue services in England take to reach fires, split into call handling, crew turnout and drive time. It was produced by the Department for Communities and Local Government and later the Home Office fire statistics team, and each release comes with data tables. Coverage is all 44 fire and rescue authorities in England, by financial year back to the mid-1990s, with average response times for primary fires in dwellings, other buildings, road vehicles and outdoor fires, and breakdowns by authority type (metropolitan, predominantly urban, significantly rural, predominantly rural). Tables are free to download as spreadsheets and PDF bulletins under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Caveats: figures are averages, not incident-level times; the method changed when the Incident Recording System replaced paper returns in 2009; and from the release for April 2023 to March 2024 the bulletin is folded into the annual detailed analysis of fires, so the stand-alone collection is no longer updated. Simulation uses: setting target response-time distributions and validating fire station coverage and emergency response models at authority scale, and comparing urban and rural service levels for resilience planning. Related records: the England fire incident-level datasets (data-england-fire-incident-level-datasets) hold the underlying incident records, and the London Fire Brigade incident records (data-london-fire-brigade-incident-records) give times per incident for London.
